title: GitHub - sib-project/sib: A standard Unix LLM client
excerpt: A standard Unix LLM client. Contribute to sib-project/sib development by creating an account on GitHub.
content_html:
I like Git a bit too much, so Sib stores LLM conversations using Git itself instead of SQLite. Your store is a plain Git repository, and each user and assistant turn is a commit.

This gives you:

  • Full control of the context. Just like git does.
  • Backup and sharing for free. The store is a normal Git repository, so any Git host works as a remote.
  • Description - introducing concept with tutorial
  • Quickstart - installation and setups
  • Tips - usage examples
  • Hacking - extending Sib as you please

Description

Typical usage:

echo 'Why did Evangelion 3.0 suddenly go off the rails?' | sib ask
sib log
echo 'Which of those two reasons matters more?' | sib ask

sib ask reads a prompt from stdin, sends it to the model along with every turn reachable from HEAD, prints the reply to stdout, and records both turns as two commits. sib log prints the whole conversation.

Now, the store looks like this:

* fa754c HEAD~3 {"role":"user", "content":"Why did Evangelion 3.0 suddenly ..."}
* b16df7 HEAD~2 {"role":"assistant", "content":"Because *Evangelion 3.0: You ..."}
* 1c2e90 HEAD~1 {"role":"user", "content":"Which of those two reasons matters ..."}
* 280f09 HEAD   {"role":"assistant", "content":"The **intentional creative ..."}

This is the overall concept. But why? It looks unnecessarily complicated.

Let's look at a command like this:

sib ask -rp HEAD~1

What each flag does:

  • -r: do not read stdin; send the chain to endpoint as is
  • -p HEAD~1: treat HEAD~1 as the parent instead of HEAD

Since your last prompt lives at HEAD~1, this is the same as the 'Repeat' button seen in the web UI.

Without -r:

echo 'So you mean the 14-year skip was a good decision?' | sib ask -p HEAD~2

This is similar to the 'Edit' button. It forks from HEAD~2, as if you edited 1c2e90 in a web UI.

* fa754c HEAD~3 {"role":"user", "content":"Why did Evangelion 3.0 suddenly ..."}
* b16df7 HEAD~2 {"role":"assistant", "content":"Because *Evangelion 3.0: You ..."}
* 32e3f4 HEAD~1 {"role":"user", "content":"So you mean the 14-year skip was a ..."}
* 8cc404 HEAD   {"role":"assistant", "content":"Artistically, yes; narratively, ..."}

Hashes are hard to remember, so name them:

sib save eva-3.0-go-off
sib save -l               # List saved names

The saved name can be addressed with -p (and other commands like sib log ...):

sib git fetch https://github.com/sib-project/hub \
    dilluti0n/why-evangelion-end-like-that:refs/conv/why-evangelion-end-like-that

sib log why-evangelion-end-like-that

echo 'learning to accept himself? Honestly speaking, did he really succeed?' \
    'Why is he being congratulated?' | sib ask -p why-evangelion-end-like-that

Each save stays in place by default and does not follow the sib ask. If the result matches the original name and you like it, save it one more time.

sib save why-evangelion-end-like-that

Your Evangelion 3.0 chain is of course still there:

sib log eva-3.0-go-off

You can pick it up again with sib ask -p. But sometimes you only want to move HEAD:

sib ask -crp eva-3.0-go-off

-c is new here: no API call, so no assistant turn. With -r there is no input either, so all that is left is moving HEAD.

These cover nearly every use case for Sib.

Knowing how conversations are saved gives you Repeat, Edit, Fork, saving conversations, and switching conversations. Backup and sharing come from the same place. Other tools ship each of them as a separate named feature. Sib does not have to.

That's why.

Quickstart

Here lies the unavoidable boilerplate you must endure to use Sib.

Dependencies are bash >= 3.2, git, jq, curl, awk and coreutils.

Download release tarball or clone this repo:

git clone https://github.com/sib-project/sib

Global install:

sudo make install

User install:

make PREFIX="$HOME/.local" install

# on macOS, add this line to .zshrc and rerun terminal
export PATH="$HOME/.local/bin:$PATH"

Init the repository:

sib init

Check defaults:

$ sib status
SIB_DIR:      /home/hskim/.sib
PLM_MODEL:    gpt-5.6-luna
PLM_ENDPOINT: https://api.openai.com/v1/responses

HEAD: (unborn)

Change the endpoint/model (defaults work out of the box for openai).

sib config edit # Inspect and edit the defaults
sib config set sib.endpoint https://api.cyberdyne.com/v1/responses
sib config set sib.model skynet-101-arnold

Export the API key:

export PLM_API_KEY='sk-xxxxxx' # Add this to ~/.bashrc to make it persist
export OPENAI_API_KEY='sk-xxxxxx' # This also works

Ask something:

echo 'Why did Evangelion end like that?' | sib ask
sib ask -rp HEAD~1 -m skynet-500   # Re-ask with other model

Now, enjoy!

Tips

Sharing

We previously fetched the conversation in the tutorial:

sib git fetch https://github.com/sib-project/hub \
    dilluti0n/nvim-sib-log-res:refs/conv/nvim-sib-log-res

The above command copies the conversation directly to your repository. You can read it with sib log nvim-sib-log-res or continue it wherever you want with sib ask -p nvim-sib-log-res.

The reverse works too:

sib git push <your-repo-url> <local-ref>:refs/heads/<remote-ref>

Wanna share yours with random internet dudes? In fact, you can publish to sib-project/hub too. Push to any public git repo as above and open a share issue. It will be automatically published.

Usage of sib ask

sib ask has a lot of flags. That is because it does a lot of things in the first place. Each flag changes one part of what it does, and they combine.

For example:

echo 'Summarize the entire context for use in the next conversation.' | sib ask
sib show -c | sib ask -nc

sib show -c prints only content field of HEAD, which is the summary just generated. -n ignores the existing HEAD, creates a new chain and switch to it. -c chains only user turns without querying the model.

So when a conversation gets too long, this starts a fresh one while carrying the context over.

Markdown rendering and emacs/neovim extension

If you need Markdown rendering:

sib log | glow -p

Or inside neovim:

{ echo Write a code which do same thing in neovim lua; echo; cat <<EOF
(defun sib-log ()
  (interactive)
  (require 'markdown-mode)

  (let ((buf (get-buffer-create "*sib*"))
        (err (get-buffer-create "*sib-error*")))
    (async-shell-command "sib log" buf err)

    (with-current-buffer buf
      (markdown-mode)
      (font-lock-ensure))

    (pop-to-buffer buf)))
EOF
} | sib ask -n

To save you API usage, I've already done it for you. Set it up with the following commands:

sib git fetch https://github.com/sib-project/hub \
    dilluti0n/nvim-sib-log-res:refs/conv/nvim-sib-log

sib show -c nvim-sib-log >> ~/.config/nvim/init.lua
nvim +SibLog

Also, I checked it does the things, but I don't really know much about Neovim or Lua. So the generated script came out at 74 lines (the elisp above is 12) and may be hard to maintain.

The nice part is, you already have the whole conversation behind it! So someone who actually knows their way around could pick it up from any turn, refactor it with AI, and upload an improved version.

Hacking

sib <cmd> execs sib-<cmd> from PATH. Every command you have used so far is just that: a script sitting next to the dispatcher.

So is yours. The hub URL above is too long to type twice:

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# sib-hub, anywhere in $PATH
exec sib git fetch https://github.com/sib-project/hub "$1:refs/conv/${1#*/}"

And run with

sib hub dilluti0n/nvim-sib-log-res
sib show nvim-sib-log-res

What makes this cheap is the plumbing underneath. A conversation is a chain of commits. Each commit's tree is a trace, a flat key-value map (role, content, model, ...) whose values are blobs.

sib rev-jsonl <chain>         Print <chain> to jsonl format
sib chain-jsonl               Chain jsonl file to sib store and print its id

sib rev-parse / show-ref / update-ref / ls-refs / symbolic-ref
sib git ...                   raw git on the store

There are other commands, but for now, the above is all you need to know.

  • A manual page is planned; if you want to write it first, see contribute.
  • The sib-ask code (49 lines excluding flag parsing) will also help.

These resources are not fully documented yet, so some of it may not be obvious. Please feel free to ask about it via email or issue tracker at any time.

Minimum rules for compatibility

  • Keys matching glob pattern _SIBTRACE* are reserved.
  • Keys must match [A-Za-z_][A-Za-z0-9._-]*.
  • The other keys don't matter except content.
  • The commit date is fixed at 999999999 +0000, with author and committer Sibyl <sib@local>. Through this, we can obtain the same hash for the same conversation chain.

The project is in its early stages. The codebase is not yet stable enough for large feature work, but you can get involved in shaping the core API.

content_html_zh:
我太喜欢 Git 了，所以 Sib 使用 Git 本身而不是 SQLite 来存储 LLM 对话。 您的商店是一个普通的 Git 存储库，每个用户和助理都是一次提交。

这给你：

  • 完全控制上下文。 就像 git 一样。
  • 免费备份和共享。 该商店是一个普通的 Git 存储库，因此任何 Git 主机都可以作为远程主机。
  • 描述 - 通过教程介绍概念
  • 快速入门 - 安装和设置
  • 提示 - 使用示例
  • 黑客攻击 - 随心所欲地扩展 Sib

描述

典型用法：

echo 'Why did Evangelion 3.0 suddenly go off the rails?' | sib ask
sib log
echo 'Which of those two reasons matters more?' | sib ask

sib Ask 从 stdin 读取提示，将其与 HEAD 可到达的每个回合一起发送到模型，将回复打印到 stdout，并将两个回合记录为两次提交。 sib log 打印整个对话。

现在，商店是这样的：

* fa754c HEAD~3 {"role":"user", "content":"Why did Evangelion 3.0 suddenly ..."}
* b16df7 HEAD~2 {"role":"assistant", "content":"Because *Evangelion 3.0: You ..."}
* 1c2e90 HEAD~1 {"role":"user", "content":"Which of those two reasons matters ..."}
* 280f09 HEAD   {"role":"assistant", "content":"The **intentional creative ..."}

这是整体的概念。 但为什么？ 它看起来不必要地复杂。

让我们看一下这样的命令：

sib ask -rp HEAD~1

每个标志的作用：

  • -r：不读取标准输入；按原样将链发送到端点
  • -p HEAD~1：将 HEAD~1 视为父级而不是 HEAD

由于您的最后一个提示位于 HEAD~1，因此这与 Web UI 中看到的“重复”按钮相同。

没有-r：

echo 'So you mean the 14-year skip was a good decision?' | sib ask -p HEAD~2

这类似于“编辑”按钮。 它从 HEAD~2 分叉，就像您在 Web UI 中编辑 1c2e90 一样。

* fa754c HEAD~3 {"role":"user", "content":"Why did Evangelion 3.0 suddenly ..."}
* b16df7 HEAD~2 {"role":"assistant", "content":"Because *Evangelion 3.0: You ..."}
* 32e3f4 HEAD~1 {"role":"user", "content":"So you mean the 14-year skip was a ..."}
* 8cc404 HEAD   {"role":"assistant", "content":"Artistically, yes; narratively, ..."}

哈希值很难记住，所以给它们命名：

sib save eva-3.0-go-off
sib save -l               # List saved names

保存的名称可以使用 -p （以及其他命令，如 sib log ...）来寻址：

sib git fetch https://github.com/sib-project/hub \
    dilluti0n/why-evangelion-end-like-that:refs/conv/why-evangelion-end-like-that

sib log why-evangelion-end-like-that

echo 'learning to accept himself? Honestly speaking, did he really succeed?' \
    'Why is he being congratulated?' | sib ask -p why-evangelion-end-like-that

默认情况下，每个保存都会保留在原处，并且不遵循同胞的要求。 如果结果与原始名称匹配并且您喜欢它，请再保存一次。

sib save why-evangelion-end-like-that

你的新世纪福音战士 3.0 链当然还在那里：

sib log eva-3.0-go-off

您可以使用 sib Ask -p 再次拾取它。 但有时你只想移动 HEAD：

sib ask -crp eva-3.0-go-off

-c 是新的：没有 API 调用，所以没有助手轮流。 使用 -r 也没有输入，所以剩下的就是移动 HEAD。

这些几乎涵盖了 Sib 的所有用例。

了解对话的保存方式后，您可以重复、编辑、分叉、保存对话和切换对话。 备份和共享来自同一个地方。 其他工具将它们作为单独的命名功能提供。 西伯不必这么做。

这就是原因。

快速入门

这是使用 Sib 时必须忍受的不可避免的样板。

依赖项为 bash >= 3.2、git、jq、curl、awk 和 coreutils。

下载发行版 tarball 或克隆此存储库：

git clone https://github.com/sib-project/sib

全局安装：

sudo make install

用户安装：

make PREFIX="$HOME/.local" install

# on macOS, add this line to .zshrc and rerun terminal
export PATH="$HOME/.local/bin:$PATH"

初始化存储库：

sib init

检查默认值：

$ sib status
SIB_DIR:      /home/hskim/.sib
PLM_MODEL:    gpt-5.6-luna
PLM_ENDPOINT: https://api.openai.com/v1/responses

HEAD: (unborn)

更改端点/模型（默认情况下 openai 开箱即用）。

sib config edit # Inspect and edit the defaults
sib config set sib.endpoint https://api.cyberdyne.com/v1/responses
sib config set sib.model skynet-101-arnold

导出 API 密钥：

export PLM_API_KEY='sk-xxxxxx' # Add this to ~/.bashrc to make it persist
export OPENAI_API_KEY='sk-xxxxxx' # This also works

问一些事情：

echo 'Why did Evangelion end like that?' | sib ask
sib ask -rp HEAD~1 -m skynet-500   # Re-ask with other model

现在，享受吧！

Tips

分享

我们之前在教程中获取了对话：

sib git fetch https://github.com/sib-project/hub \
    dilluti0n/nvim-sib-log-res:refs/conv/nvim-sib-log-res

上面的命令将对话直接复制到您的存储库。 您可以使用 sib log nvim-sib-log-res 读取它，或者使用 sib Ask -p nvim-sib-log-res 继续它。

反过来也有效：

sib git push <your-repo-url> <local-ref>:refs/heads/<remote-ref>

想与随机的互联网家伙分享您的吗？ 事实上，您也可以发布到 sib-project/hub。 如上所述推送到任何公共 git 存储库并打开共享问题。 它将自动发布。

同胞询问的用法

sib Ask 有很多标志。 那是因为它首先做了很多事情。 每个标志都会更改其功能的一部分，然后将它们组合起来。

例如：

echo 'Summarize the entire context for use in the next conversation.' | sib ask
sib show -c | sib ask -nc

sib show -c 仅打印 HEAD 的内容字段，这是刚刚生成的摘要。 -n 忽略现有的 HEAD，创建一个新链并切换到它。 -c 仅链接用户轮次而不查询模型。

因此，当对话变得太长时，就会开始新的对话，同时延续上下文。

Markdown 渲染和 emacs/neovim 扩展

如果需要Markdown渲染：

sib log | glow -p

或者在 neovim 中：

{ echo Write a code which do same thing in neovim lua; echo; cat <<EOF
(defun sib-log ()
  (interactive)
  (require 'markdown-mode)

  (let ((buf (get-buffer-create "*sib*"))
        (err (get-buffer-create "*sib-error*")))
    (async-shell-command "sib log" buf err)

    (with-current-buffer buf
      (markdown-mode)
      (font-lock-ensure))

    (pop-to-buffer buf)))
EOF
} | sib ask -n

为了节省您的 API 使用量，我已经为您完成了。 使用以下命令进行设置：

sib git fetch https://github.com/sib-project/hub \
    dilluti0n/nvim-sib-log-res:refs/conv/nvim-sib-log

sib show -c nvim-sib-log >> ~/.config/nvim/init.lua
nvim +SibLog

另外，我检查了它的功能，但我对 Neovim 或 Lua 不太了解。 所以生成的脚本有 74 行（上面的 elisp 是 12 行），并且可能很难维护。

令人高兴的是，您已经掌握了整个对话的内容！ 因此，真正了解方法的人可以从任何回合中拿起它，用人工智能重构它，并上传改进的版本。

黑客攻击

sib <cmd> 从 PATH 执行 sib-<cmd>。 到目前为止，您使用的每个命令都只是：位于调度程序旁边的脚本。

你的也是如此。 上面的中心 URL 太长，无法输入两次：

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# sib-hub, anywhere in $PATH
exec sib git fetch https://github.com/sib-project/hub "$1:refs/conv/${1#*/}"

并运行

sib hub dilluti0n/nvim-sib-log-res
sib show nvim-sib-log-res

之所以这么便宜，是因为下面的管道。 对话是一系列提交。 每个提交的树都是一个跟踪，一个平面键值映射（角色、内容、模型……） 其值是 blob。

sib rev-jsonl <chain>         Print <chain> to jsonl format
sib chain-jsonl               Chain jsonl file to sib store and print its id

sib rev-parse / show-ref / update-ref / ls-refs / symbolic-ref
sib git ...                   raw git on the store

还有其他命令，但目前您只需要了解以上内容即可。

  • 计划提供手册页；如果你想先写，请参阅contribution。
  • sib-ask 代码（49 行，不包括标志解析）也会有所帮助。

这些资源尚未完整记录，因此其中一些可能并不明显。 请随时通过电子邮件或问题跟踪器询问。

兼容性的最低规则

  • 保留与 glob 模式 _SIBTRACE* 匹配的键。
  • 键必须匹配 [A-Za-z_][A-Za-z0-9._-]*。
  • 除了内容之外，其他键都不重要。
  • 提交日期固定为 999999999 +0000，作者和提交者为 Sibyl <sib@local>。 通过这个，我们可以获得同一条会话链的相同哈希值。

该项目正处于早期阶段。 代码库对于大型功能工作来说还不够稳定，但您可以参与塑造核心 API。
